title: WHO Member States continue negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing Annex
date_evidence:
# WHO Member States continue negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing Annex

20 July 2026

News release

Geneva
key_claim: The seventh IGWG meeting (6-17 July 2026, Geneva) closed without a finished PABS annex. Unresolved items are the contractual arrangements, the laboratory-network structure for handling pathogens and their sequence information, and the definition of benefits. An eighth meeting runs 14-18 September 2026, and finalising the annex remains the precondition for signature and ratification.
frame_summary: WHO is arguing that PABS talks are advancing constructively and the remaining gaps are bridgeable, while conceding the annex, and therefore the Agreement's entry into force, is still unfinished after a fourth negotiating round in 2026.
verbatim_quote: The meeting concluded with Member States reaffirming their commitment to continue intensive negotiations toward an ambitious, effective and equitable PABS annex. Finalizing the annex is a critical step toward enabling countries to consider the signature and ratification of the WHO Pandemic Agreement, strengthening global health security and pandemic prevention, preparedness and response for future generations.
verbatim_list: The IGWG will hold its eighth meeting from 14-18 September 2026.

Discussions focused on several interrelated elements of the PABS system, including the contractual arrangements underpinning the framework, the structure of the laboratory networks responsible for the sharing and handling of pathogens with pandemic potential and their sequence information, and the definition of benefits arising from pathogen sharing.
notes: Primary institutional record of the July 2026 round. The WHO page is JS-rendered and exposes no article:published_time; the date was read off the visible dateline beneath the headline. Live-verified via WebFetch on 2026-07-26; the sandbox provenance audit cannot fetch who.int, so quote_provenance is manually-verified.

title: Les Etats Membres de l'OMS conviennent de prolonger les negociations concernant l'annexe sur le systeme d'acces aux agents pathogenes et de partage des avantages
date_evidence:
Les Etats Membres de l'OMS conviennent de prolonger les negociations ... 1 mai 2026

Communique de presse

Geneve
key_claim: At the close of the resumed sixth IGWG session on 1 May 2026, Member States asked the World Health Assembly to extend the mandate under resolution WHA78.1, with the outcome to be submitted in May 2027 or earlier at a special session in 2026. WHO states that finalising the PABS annex is a precondition for signature and ratification.
frame_summary: WHO is arguing that the extension reflects seriousness rather than failure, while stating on the record that the Pandemic Agreement cannot be signed or ratified until the PABS annex is finished.
verbatim_quote: Il est nécessaire de finaliser l’annexe PABS pour que les pays puissent procéder à la signature et à la ratification de l’Accord sur les pandémies.
verbatim_list: Compte tenu de la nécessité de poursuivre les négociations, l’Assemblée sera priée d’envisager la poursuite des travaux du Groupe de travail intergouvernemental tel que prévu dans la résolution WHA78.1 et de présenter les résultats de ces travaux à la prochaine Assemblée en mai 2027, ou plus tôt, à l’occasion d’une session extraordinaire de l’Assemblée mondiale de la Santé en 2026.
notes: Multi-language source: Tier 1, French, published by WHO/OMS in Geneva. Full official translation, not machine-rendered (og:locale fr_FR). verified_at is set to the publication timestamp because the French page carries no separate verification marker; content live-verified via WebFetch on 2026-07-26.

publisher: The Independent Panel for Pandemic Preparedness and Response
title: The events of 2026 show why the world cannot wait to deliver the PABS Annex
key_claim: The Panel's statement to IGWG7 links the unfinished annex to two live 2026 events: the late-April hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius and the Bundibugyo Ebola public health emergency of international concern declared on 17 May 2026.
frame_summary: The Panel is arguing that real outbreaks in the first half of 2026 have already stress-tested the gaps PABS is meant to close, so the negotiating delay carries an operational rather than merely diplomatic cost.
verbatim_quote: We urge negotiators to seize the next two weeks and take a major step towards the finish line: a PABS system which guarantees timely access and equitable benefit sharing, in line with the provisions set out in Article 12.
verbatim_list: Just three weeks later, on 17 May, the WHO Director-General declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern linked to the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak.
In late April, the hantavirus outbreak linked to the MV Hondius vessel became an early stress test for the international system.
notes: Co-chaired by Ellen Johnson Sirleaf and Helen Clark. Tier 2 as an independent expert panel rather than a Member State body. Live-verified via WebFetch on 2026-07-26.

title: PABS Negotiations: Legal Certainty and Equity Must Define the Final Outcome
key_claim: The operative fight is the de-linking of access from benefit-sharing. The EU's blended model, tabled after IGWG6 in March 2026, would create a dual track in which one route allows free, unconditional transfer of pathogens and sequence information with no benefit-sharing obligation. The Pandemic Agreement itself provides a 10 percent donation set-aside during pandemic emergencies plus a non-binding expectation of up to another 10 percent at affordable price.
frame_summary: This piece is arguing that developed-country proposals are backsliding from Article 12 and would produce a system in which biological materials flow freely while benefits remain contingent.
verbatim_quote: The PA provides for a limited set-aside of VTDs — 10 percent donation — during pandemic emergencies, with a further expectation (non-binding) that up to another 10 percent would be reserved for WHO at an affordable price.
verbatim_list: Under this model, one track allows Free and unconditional transfer of pathogens and access to sequence information without benefit-sharing or other obligations, while another requires user registration and contractual arrangements for the transfer of pathogens, access to sequence information, and sharing of benefits.
Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and Japan, however, continue to oppose fixed percentages in any such provision.
Moreover, the negotiating leverage of resource providers and the WHO is strongest at the point of access; once resources have been utilised, that leverage diminishes significantly.
notes: Treat directionally: the author, Nithin Ramakrishan, is a senior researcher with Third World Network, aligned with the Global South negotiating position, so the piece is argumentative rather than neutral reporting. The 10 plus 10 percent figure is independently corroborated by the Health Policy Watch 17 June 2026 source in this set. Live-verified via WebFetch on 2026-07-26.

title: PABS Annex to the WHO Pandemic Agreement: Member States extend negotiations into 2027
key_claim: The 27 April to 1 May 2026 session failed to produce agreement before the World Health Assembly because differences between the Africa Group and Group for Equity on one side and industrialised countries including EU Member States on the other remained too substantial; the annex is now expected no later than the Assembly in May 2027.
frame_summary: KAS is arguing that the extension shows Member States refusing to compress a legally and technically complex system into a premature compromise, a deliberately non-alarmist reading of the delay.
verbatim_quote: Although the negotiations did not yet result in the agreement that many had hoped for, at least, WHO Member States agreed to submit a draft decision to WHA79 that would allow work on the PABS Annex to continue. The next formal IGWG session is scheduled to take place from 6 to 17 July 2026, with the Annex expected to be resubmitted no later than the World Health Assembly in May 2027.
verbatim_list: Differences between negotiating groups remained too substantial, particularly between many developing and emerging economies, through the Africa Group and the Group for Equity, and several industrialised countries, including the EU Member States.

The PABS Annex to the WHO Pandemic Agreement is intended to give operational and legal form to a multilateral system for the rapid, safe and traceable sharing of pathogen materials and related sequence information, while ensuring that such access is linked to fair and reliable benefit-sharing.
notes: German political foundation with a permanent Geneva multilateral-affairs office; the Geneva Telegram is its standing Geneva-process briefing series, author Linde Buder. The page cited is the English edition of a German original. Live-verified via WebFetch on 2026-07-26.

title: Despite Delays, Negotiations Over Critical PABS Annex to WHO Pandemic Treaty Reveal Signs of Progress
key_claim: Counter-evidence. Four Geneva Graduate Institute Global Health Centre authors argue the near-total absence of agreed green text is misleading: delegates have converged on WHO-coordinated laboratory networks and WHO-recognised sequence databases as the backbone, a hybrid registration compromise is on the table, and the May 2026 Assembly decision mandated work to develop legally binding contracts. The 20 percent real-time provision target was already settled in the 2025 Agreement.
frame_summary: This piece is arguing that the delay masks genuine substantive convergence and that the PABS annex is on track to land, the strongest available case that the slippage is procedural rather than a sign of breakdown.
verbatim_quote: While the near total absence of ‘green text’ (indicating consensus) in the latest draft left the impression that little headway has been made, that may be misleading. A look back at countries’ original proposals, and the evolution of negotiations over the past year, shows that progress has been significant, even if deep divisions remain.
verbatim_list: While the 20% target for the real-time provision of products for pandemic emergencies was enshrined in the 2025 Pandemic Agreement – other types of proposed in-kind and monetary contributions have remained a sticking point in the PABS debate.

Notably, the May 2026 WHA decision extending the PABS talks included in its scope of work a mandate for member states to find agreement “to develop legally binding contracts,” a priority for the Global South, even if the content of those contracts remains a point of debate.

Most importantly, after 9 months, a clearer common understanding of how the overall system could work seems to be emerging, with WHO-coordinated laboratory networks and WHO-recognized sequence databases comprising the backbone.
notes: Designated counter-evidence source. Authors: Suerie Moon, Adam Strobeyko, Daniela Morich and Gian Luca Burci of the Global Health Centre, Geneva Graduate Institute; Tier 2 calibre analysts publishing through a Tier 3 outlet, tiered here by publisher. Live-verified via WebFetch on 2026-07-26.

title: Pandemic Agreement on Hold: Can Countries Bridge the Divide on Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing?
key_claim: The canonical framing: the Pandemic Agreement will not be opened for signature until the PABS annex is completed, an uncommon feature in international law that halts entry into force. Around 100 low- and middle-income countries demand mandatory benefit-sharing as the price of rapid pathogen-information sharing, and the draft expanded from seven pages to 37 as delegations reinserted deleted language.
frame_summary: This piece is arguing that PABS is stalled by a North-South split over whether benefit-sharing is mandatory or voluntary, and that United States bilateral pathogen-for-aid deals are corroding the multilateral system from outside.
verbatim_quote: Although adopted, the Agreement will not be opened for signature until a supplementary Annex on the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing (PABS) system is completed—an uncommon feature in international law that temporarily halts the Agreement’s progress toward entry into force until the details of the Annex are agreed.
verbatim_list: A bloc of approximately 100 low-and middle-income countries (LMICs) continues to call for mandatory benefit sharing, including guaranteed LMIC access to vaccines, therapeutics, and diagnostics (VTDs) as the price of their rapid sharing of information on novel pathogens that might pose a pandemic risk.
As a result, the document expanded from seven pages to 37, producing a dense and unwieldy “rolling text” in which every proposal reappeared.
In these arrangements, seen as a cornerstone of the new US global health policy, aid and commercial deals are offered in exchange for access to pathogen samples and data about disease outbreaks.
In August, WHO Member States submitted 17 textual proposals reflecting the views of approximately 100 countries.
notes: Structural anchor: the single source in the 3-6 month band, published 27 January 2026, one day inside the 180-day window. Author Daniela Morich, head of policy engagement at the Geneva Graduate Institute Global Health Centre. Live-verified via WebFetch on 2026-07-26.

publisher: International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations
title: Statement on PABS Instrument at the seventh meeting of the Intergovernmental Working Group on the WHO Pandemic Agreement
date_evidence:
Statement 6 July 2026

## Statement on PABS Instrument at the seventh meeting of the Intergovernmental Working Group (IGWG 7) on the WHO Pandemic Agreement
key_claim: Industry states that mandatory monetary contributions and other PABS obligations would weaken already thin emerging-infectious-disease research pipelines, and reports an observed shift during outbreak response away from open-access data systems toward restricted-use arrangements.
frame_summary: IFPMA is arguing that PABS as drafted would price and gate pathogen access in a way that slows rather than speeds outbreak response, and that negotiators should build on existing voluntary open-sharing mechanisms instead.
verbatim_quote: Recent experience shows a clear shift away from open access systems historically used in outbreaks, toward more restricted-use arrangements.
verbatim_list: Introducing mandatory monetary contributions and other obligations would risk further weakening these pipelines by diverting scarce resources, disincentivizing investment and likely reduce company involvement.

Instead, we should build on existing mechanisms that already enable rapid, open, and effective data sharing, including established international databases, while ensuring that countries are supported and enabled to operationalize agreed access provisions.
notes: Treat directionally: industry trade association, used only as corroboration of direction of travel, not as an independent factual authority. Its value is as the clearest on-record confirmation that the manufacturers who would owe the set-aside regard mandatory contributions as a research disincentive, and that sharing behaviour is already becoming more restricted. Live-verified via WebFetch on 2026-07-26.
